name: Abda
title: Father of Adoniram, overseer of the forced laborers under Solomon
summary: Abda is known from the Old Testament as the father of Adoniram, the official who had supervision over the forced laborers during King Solomon's reign. The name Abda is an Aramaized form of the Hebrew word for 'servant', and can be understood as a short form of a theophoric name meaning 'God's servant'. Although Abda is primarily known through his son, his place in the biblical text indicates that the family held a prominent role in the administration of the united kingdom under Solomon.

keyEvents.title: Abda's son Adoniram as Solomon's official
keyEvents.description: Abda is mentioned as the father of Adoniram, who was responsible for the forced laborers during King Solomon's rule. This shows that Abda's family held an important position in Israel's administration.

keyEvents.title: Adoram's service under David
keyEvents.description: In 2 Samuel 20:24, an Adoram is mentioned as the overseer of the forced laborers under King David. Several scholars identify this Adoram with Adoniram son of Abda, but the identification is uncertain. If it is the same person, his career spanned the reigns of two kings.

keyEvents.title: Adoram's tragic death
keyEvents.description: An official named Adoram – possibly identical to Adoniram son of Abda, or a successor in the same office – was stoned to death by the people of Israel when King Rehoboam sent him to collect forced labor. The event marked the final division of the kingdom.

footnotes.text: The name Abda (עַבְדָּא) is an Aramaic form of the Hebrew עֶבֶד (eved), meaning 'servant' or 'slave'. It can also be understood as a shortened form of a theophoric name meaning 'God's servant'. This type of name was common in the ancient Near East and appears in several Semitic languages.

The forced labor system (Heb. mas) that Adoniram led was a central part of Solomon's building projects, including the temple and the royal palace. The system required Israelites to perform compulsory labor for set periods. It was highly controversial and became one of the main causes of the kingdom's division after Solomon's death (1 Kings 12).

Scholars debate whether Adoram mentioned in 2 Samuel 20:24 (under David) and Adoniram son of Abda in 1 Kings 4:6 (under Solomon) are the same person. If they are, he would have had an unusually long career spanning several kings' reigns, which would testify to the stability and importance of the office.

There is another person named Abda mentioned in Nehemiah 11:17—a Levite who lived in Jerusalem after the exile. This Abda must not be confused with Abda, father of Adoniram, who lived several hundred years earlier during the time of the united kingdom.
